title: Quadriplegia, paraplegia, monoplegia and spinal cord disorders
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's paralysis or spinal cord condition (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for cervical spondylotic myelopathy.

HPI
The patient is a 68-year-old man presenting for a follow-up evaluation regarding his cervical spondylosis with myelopathy. He reports that his symptoms have been stable since his recent spine surgery. He denies any new episodes of numbness, tingling, or significant motor weakness in his upper extremities. He notes that his gait feels steady and he is managing well with his current rehabilitation routine. He reports minimal persistent discomfort following the surgical intervention.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 40mg daily
Gabapentin 300mg twice daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. He appears in no acute distress. Neurological exam shows intact sensation to light touch and pinprick in all four extremities. Motor strength is 5/5 in the upper and lower extremities. Reflexes are symmetric and 2+ throughout. No new gait abnormalities noted during observation.

Assessment
1. Cervical spondylotic myelopathy status post spine surgery.

Plan
The patient will continue his current medication regimen and physical therapy. He is instructed to monitor for any new neurological deficits. We will follow up in six weeks for a repeat clinical evaluation.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, PA-C, 10/14/2026
explanations: Cervical spondylosis with myelopathy has a combination code: M47.12 (no HCC). Unspecified spinal cord disease (G95.9) would add HCC 182.
